subject: general
question: In a code language, 'BRACKET' is written as ‘VGMECTD’ and 'PLUSH' is written as 'JUWNR'. How will 'VIABLE' be written in that language?
solution:
The positional value table is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/889ff2be8a048327f450a975a401b2f4241e5f28d86896613386ad4014cb4505.png] 

The pattern followed here is:

**Letters are increasing by +2 and written backwards.**

 
• In BRACKET → VGMECTD 

 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ca6b448673837742e64a83a8aa7b1c790cff77197759bf2e708a82cb8a4c945.png] 
 
• Written backwards = 'VGMECTD'​​​.
 
 

 

 
• In PLUSH → JUWNR ​

 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffe6c8d875e8be59bf312b470b343ecd1531f6d38a0c4454626dbaad7461918a.png] 
 
• Written backwards = 'JUWNR'​​​.
 
 

 

 
• Similarly, In **VIABLE** → ​

 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad2d69323ac2764a36d86b9d963bc9cc0d847261cc4783e3560c5e6b50791696.png] 
 
• Written backwards = '**GNDCKX'**
 
 

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.
